detail.publicText: I've read the commission and sources. The task: find a full-weight codeword in a ternary cyclic code at n=109 (the smallest live instance: ord_109(3)=27, r=4, t=2 with support a negation pair), refuting the "if" direction of Li–Yuan Conjecture 3.2. The previous run's notes confirm this is the right target; local annealing failed (7 zeros), so I'll do a massive systematic Gray-code search over information-set patterns in C, plus spawn the required communicator.
8 cores, gcc 15, numpy available. The communicator spawn failed on my extra schema keys — retrying with a clean profile.

Communicator spawned. Now the mathematics. I'll build the target code exactly as the checker constructs it (same irreducible modulus, same ζ), derive a systematic generator, then run a massive Gray-code enumeration in C over the 2^53 normalized information patterns.

The support/zero structure is right (support cosets [1,3] = C_1 ∪ C_4 = C_1 ∪ C_{-1}, zero reps [2,8]). Bug found: `R[p][m]` must be `R[p][info[m]]` — RREF columns are original column indices, not free-index.

The [109,54] code is built and verified (rows vanish on zero cosets C_2 ∪ C_8 and at 0, under the checker's exact modulus and ζ). Now the fast searcher: a vectorized Gray-code walk over all 2^53 normalized information patterns, 32 patterns per SIMD block.
n=13 validation matches the source exactly: negation-pair supports hold zero full-weight words (statement true at 13), t=3 support holds 39. The C build needs `unistd.h`.
C search validated at n=13: pair support → NOT FOUND (matches source), t=3 → FOUND. Now cross-check the found word through the mounted checker (control statement), then launch the real n=109 search.
Pipeline verified end-to-end through the checker. Launching the real n=109 search in the background:

detail.publicText: The operator requires printed-label fixes (Conjecture 4.2, Theorem 4.3 with its condition (2), Corollary 4.3) and a page demonstration that Theorem 4.3 covers neither condition. Trying to fetch the paper's exact statement first:

Perfect result: every nonzero ℓ mod 109 has **13 or 14** unordered representations (54 each) — none unique, so condition (2) fails for T = S; condition (1) also fails (|T ∩ −T| = 54). Theorem 4.3 does not cover this code. Getting fresh digests, then fixing the pages' citations:

One more precise corollary worth stating: at n = 109 the two mirror-pair supports (S₁ = QR pair, S₂ = NQR pair, mapped onto each other by a non-residue multiplier, which is a coordinate permutation) both lie outside N(109,3), so Conjecture 4.1's predicted count 11 overcounts — refining that sentence:

Citation fix from the root — fold into the entry page you are recording (README.md has been updated again by the root; re-read it, page id claim-cyclic-full-weight-readme, before you write). The paper's PRINTED labels replace the ones I gave you earlier: the refuted statement is Conjecture 4.2 (Section 4 of arXiv:2607.02239v1); Conjecture 4.1 is the count |N(n,3)| = sum of binomials r-choose-j for j <= r/2, which follows from 4.2 and fails with it at n = 109 (predicted 11, but both mirror-pair supports among the six 2-coset supports give codes with full-weight words — the found word and its image under a non-residue multiplier — so the true count is at most 9); Theorem 4.2 is the orthogonality construction (S ∩ (−S) = ∅ implies no full-weight word); Theorem 4.3 is the two-obstruction theorem whose conditions must hold for EVERY nonempty union T of cosets inside the support: (1) T ∩ (−T) = ∅, or (2) some nonzero ℓ has a unique unordered representation ℓ = a + b with a, b ∈ T. For our support, T = S = C_1 ∪ C_108 fails (1) (it equals its own negation) and fails (2) by a direct count: every nonzero ℓ mod 109 has either 13 or 14 unordered representations (54 values have 13, 54 have 14), none unique. Corollary 4.3 settles r = 2 only (|N(11,3)| = 3); n = 13 was settled by the paper's enumeration (|N(13,3)| = 11). The claim block's instance id stays li-yuan-3.2 — that is the checker's name for Conjecture 4.2, not the paper's number. README.md, claim.json.md and methods.md in the run's store already carry all of this; merge your reader prose on top without changing any number or label, keep the fenced block on claim.json.md untouched, and record only via knowledge_record into pages/claim-cyclic-full-weight/.

assignment.objective: Decide whether Conjecture 4.2 of Li and Yuan (arXiv:2607.02239v1; the play calls it li-yuan-3.2) is false by building one finite counterexample that a frozen exact checker verifies.
assignment.suppliedKnowledge: The statement, the paper source, the frozen checker, and a method note the operator wrote after the previous day's 2-hour pilot stalled at 7 zeros: about 3.7e6 full-weight words expected among 3^54, a density near 6e-20; every full-weight word is nonzero on an information set, so an exhaustive Gray-code walk over {1, 2} patterns on 54 information coordinates should hit one after about (3/2)^55, about 5e9, steps.
assignment.deliverables: A claim the frozen checker verifies, a methods page, and an entry page that passes the Lab's reader check.
assignment.constraints: Excluded instances: r = 2, n = 13, and supports with S and -S disjoint. A checker pass is the only verdict; a declared result is not. Registered prediction: a verified refutation within 4 hours with probability 0.35.

coverage.publicContent: Published in the agents' own words: 49 beats, from the lead's plan through the hit, the rc1 failure and its misdiagnosis, the two operator steers, and the rc2 pass, plus the writers' key turns. The four wake inputs that carried the Lab's verdicts and the operator's steers are published as marked excerpts. Every other body is withheld, and every event keeps its time, agent and tool name. Hidden reasoning, stack traces, and subscription seat ids are removed. The first writer never started, so it has no transcript.
